paragraphs: In Yevamot 64b: she was the daughter of Issi, son of Rav Yitzchak, son of Rav Yehudah. Rechava of Pumbedita married her and died; Rav Yitzchak son of Rabbah bar bar Chana married her and died. Rav Yitzchak bar Yosef came and related before Abaye that Rabbi Yochanan holds that a presumption is established only after three times; on this basis Abaye went and married her, and he too died. Rava said: “Is there anyone who would act on himself like this?” Ketubot 65a relates that she came before Rava and said to him, “Fix maintenance for me”; he fixed it for her. “Fix wine for me.” He said to her: “I know that Nachmani did not drink wine.” She said to him: “By the Master’s life, he used to give me to drink from cups like this.” As she was showing him, her arm was exposed, and light fell upon the courtroom (for she was exceedingly beautiful and her flesh shone). Rava rose and went home and sought [relations] with Rav Chisda’s daughter (his wife) … Rava’s wife went out after Chumah and beat her with the bar of a chest until she drove her out of all of Mechoza, saying to her: “You have killed three, and you have come to kill another?”

notes.text: Nachmani is Abaye. Rava’s wife, the daughter of Chisda, is the woman who follows and strikes Chumah; the pronoun chain is made explicit without changing the supplied three-death account.

The complete inspected Ketubot 65a episode distinguishes Chumah, Rava and Rava’s wife, the daughter of Chisda, who follows and strikes Chumah. The quoted three-death accusation remains part of the narrative. The earlier marriages and genealogy remain Hyman’s supplied Yevamot account, without a new genealogy admission.
